hook.text: Every oath sworn in the town's history is being called in — oldest first: the founding families' pledge to "keep the ford free to all" enforced itself last week, dissolving toll rights held for centuries — and the enforcement is working forward through the archive toward the present.
hook.pressure: The town's order rests on generations of quietly broken vows, and everyone with property is doing frantic archival math; the guild's charter oaths come due within the month; and the NPC — whose family, the records show, swore the town's very first oath — cannot find in any archive what it actually said.
hook.ifIgnored: The enforcement reaches the present and every living oath snaps taut at once — marriages, apprenticeships, drunken vows at the tavern rail — a town suddenly run by its own given word, no clause forgiven. And at the last, the founding oath surfaces to be honored: sworn by the NPC's ancestor, binding the family line to a duty the town has needed exactly once before, and will need again by winter.

hook.text: The NPC has fallen for the portrait-sitter who comes Thursdays — married, charming, and exactly aware of it. The sittings have stretched to three hours, and the portrait has been "nearly done" since spring.
hook.pressure: The spouse commissioned the portrait as an anniversary gift — due at the feast — and has started asking why it takes so long. The sitter books another session, and another, and pays double for a silence that was never discussed.
hook.ifIgnored: The portrait is unveiled at the feast: perfect, loving, and unmistakably painted by someone besotted. Everyone at the table reads it in one look — including the spouse.

distantWord.text: Distortion — Every teller in the room somehow agrees on a detail that isn't in the ledger at all. — The fact is bound and real; this one specific added detail didn't come from it — and nobody can say where it did.
